title: Defenestrator
description: Claude subscription usage as sampled by the defenestrator (https://github.com/justmytwospence/defenestrator): account-wide 5-hour and 7-day utilization, window starts, caps, and a log of every decision it made and why. Data: the defenestrator_usage and defenestrator_event measurements in InfluxDB. Codex has its own board.

list.name: Started by defenestrator
list.query:
import "array"
import "date"
import "internal/debug"

windows = from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and (r._field == "u5" or r._field == "reset5" or r._field == "reset7"))
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.u5 and exists r.reset5 and exists r.reset7)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with win: int(v: r.reset5 / 600.0 + 0.5)}))
  |> group(columns: ["win"])
  |> max(column: "u5")
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: 1, win: r.win, peak: r.u5, wreset: r.reset5, week: int(v: r.reset7 / 43200.0 + 0.5)}))

pings = from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -1y)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_event" and r.provider == "claude" and r.kind == "ping" and r._field == "reset")
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: 1, preset: r._value}))

firstEvent = from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -1y)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_event" and r._field == "reason")
  |> group()
  |> first()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: 1, since: float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0}))

withPings = union(tables: [pings, array.from(rows: [{k: 1, preset: 0.0}])])

matched = join(tables: {w: windows, p: withPings}, on: ["k"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: r.k, win: r.win, peak: r.peak, wreset: r.wreset, week: r.week, hit: if r.preset > 0.0 and r.preset - r.wreset < 1800.0 and r.wreset - r.preset < 1800.0 then 1 else 0}))
  |> group(columns: ["win"])
  |> max(column: "hit")
  |> group()

// who started each window: defenestrator (a ping's reset matches this window's), you (events were
// being logged and no ping matches), or unknown (the window is from before events were logged)
classified = join(tables: {a: matched, b: firstEvent}, on: ["k"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({win: r.win, peak: r.peak, week: r.week, start: r.wreset - 18000.0,
      who: if r.hit == 1 then "defenestrator" else if r.wreset - 18000.0 >= r.since then "you" else "unknown"}))

classified
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.who == "defenestrator")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: time(v: int(v: r.start) * 1000000000), _value: "Defenestrator started a window, peak " + string(v: int(v: r.peak)) + "%"}))

panels.title: 5-hour window used
panels.description: Account-wide (every device) 5-hour utilization at the last sample.

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -2d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and r._field == "u5")
  |> last()

panels.title: 7-day window used
panels.description: Account-wide weekly utilization at the last sample. Defenestrator does not change weekly caps.

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -2d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and r._field == "u7")
  |> last()

panels.title: 5-hour window resets
panels.description: When the current 5-hour window ends. In the past means no window is running (the next ping or your own use starts one).

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -2d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and r._field == "reset5")
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value: r._value * 1000.0}))

panels.title: Last sample age
panels.description: Age of the newest usage sample. The timer samples every 10 minutes; older than an hour means the sampler is failing (journalctl --user -u defenestrator, or an expired Claude OAuth token).

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -2d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and r._field == "u5")
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value: float(v: int(v: now()) - int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0}))

panels.title: 5-hour utilization (last 2 days)
panels.description: Account-wide 5-hour usage. The dashed line is an even pace from 0% at the window start to 100% at its reset; the red band is where usage is above it, i.e. you are burning faster than the window allows.

panels.title: Windows started per day
panels.description: A new 5-hour window shows as a jump of about 5 hours in the reset time between samples. Counts windows however they started (a ping or your own use), so more windows a day is the point of the defenestrator.

targets.query:
import "timezone"
import "date"

option location = timezone.location(name: "America/Denver")

from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and r._field == "reset5")
  |> difference(nonNegative: false)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._value > 600.0)
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1d, fn: count, createEmpty: true, timeSrc: "_start")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value: if exists r._value then r._value else 0}))
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "windows started"})
  |> map(fn: (r) => {
      day = date.truncate(t: r._time, unit: 1d)
      names = ["Sun", "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat"]
      return {r with day: names[date.weekDay(t: day)] + " " + string(v: date.month(t: day)) + "/" + string(v: date.monthDay(t: day))}
    })
  |> keep(columns: ["day", "windows started"])

panels.title: Peak 5-hour utilization per day
panels.description: Highest 5-hour utilization sampled each day; days near 100 are where a window ran out.

panels.description: Weekly usage against a straight line from 0% at the last weekly reset to 100% at the next. The red band is where usage is above the line: you are burning faster than an even pace.

panels.description: When the weekly window resets.

panels.title: 5-hour: projected at reset
panels.description: Where this window ends up if usage continues at its rate over the last 90 minutes of the same window. 100 or more means you will hit the cap before it resets. Without a running window it shows the last value.

targets.query:
import "array"

now_s = float(v: int(v: now())) / 1000000000.0

from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -90m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and (r._field == "u5" or r._field == "reset5"))
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.u5 and exists r.reset5 and r.reset5 > now_s)
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> reduce(identity: {n: 0, u0: 0.0, t0: 0.0, u1: 0.0, t1: 0.0, reset: 0.0},
            fn: (r, accumulator) => ({n: accumulator.n + 1,
                                      u0: if accumulator.n == 0 then r.u5 else accumulator.u0,
                                      t0: if accumulator.n == 0 then float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0 else accumulator.t0,
                                      u1: r.u5, t1: float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0, reset: r.reset5}))
  |> map(fn: (r) => {
      slope = if r.t1 > r.t0 and r.u1 > r.u0 then (r.u1 - r.u0) / (r.t1 - r.t0) else 0.0
      return {_time: now(), _value: r.u1 + slope * (r.reset - now_s)}
    })

panels.title: 7-day: projected at reset
panels.description: Where the week ends up if usage continues at its rate over the last 48 hours of this week (since the last weekly reset). 100 or more means you are on course to hit the weekly cap.

targets.query:
import "array"

now_s = float(v: int(v: now())) / 1000000000.0

from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -48h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and (r._field == "u7" or r._field == "reset7"))
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.u7 and exists r.reset7 and r.reset7 > now_s)
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  |> reduce(identity: {n: 0, u0: 0.0, t0: 0.0, u1: 0.0, t1: 0.0, reset: 0.0},
            fn: (r, accumulator) => ({n: accumulator.n + 1,
                                      u0: if accumulator.n == 0 then r.u7 else accumulator.u0,
                                      t0: if accumulator.n == 0 then float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0 else accumulator.t0,
                                      u1: r.u7, t1: float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0, reset: r.reset7}))
  |> map(fn: (r) => {
      slope = if r.t1 > r.t0 and r.u1 > r.u0 then (r.u1 - r.u0) / (r.t1 - r.t0) else 0.0
      return {_time: now(), _value: r.u1 + slope * (r.reset - now_s)}
    })

panels.title: Window fill rate vs safe rate
panels.description: How fast the 5-hour window fills, in percentage points per hour (resets excluded). The dashed line is the safe rate: what you could keep using from now and still land on exactly 100% at the reset ((100 - used) / hours left). Above it you will hit the cap before the window resets.

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and r._field == "u5")
  |> derivative(unit: 1h, nonNegative: false)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._value >= 0.0)
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 30m, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> group()
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "points per hour"})

from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and (r._field == "u5" or r._field == "reset5"))
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.u5 and exists r.reset5)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, _value: (100.0 - r.u5) / ((r.reset5 - float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0) / 3600.0), left: (r.reset5 - float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0) / 3600.0}))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.left > 1.0)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 30m, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> group()
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "safe rate"})

panels.title: Average utilization by hour of day (host local time)
panels.description: Mean 5-hour utilization at each local hour over the last 28 days (ignores the dashboard range): when you are usually working.

targets.query:
import "timezone"
import "date"

option location = timezone.location(name: "America/Denver")

from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -28d)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and r._field == "u5")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with hour: date.hour(t: r._time)}))
  |> group(columns: ["hour"])
  |> mean()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["hour"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({hour: if r.hour < 10 then "0" + string(v: r.hour) else string(v: r.hour), "mean 5-hour utilization": r._value}))

panels.title: Hours capped per day
panels.description: Time the account was rate limited each day, counted as 10 minutes per capped sample.

targets.query:
import "timezone"
import "date"

option location = timezone.location(name: "America/Denver")

from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)

    })
  |> keep(columns: ["day", "_value"])
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "hours capped"})

panels.title: Decision log
panels.description: Every decision the defenestrator recorded, newest first: pings it sent, waits and plans, running windows, skips and errors (token expired, not logged in). Repeating states are recorded when they change.

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_event" and r._field == "reason" and r.provider != "codex")
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 200)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({time: r._time, provider: r.provider, kind: r.kind, reason: r._value}))

panels.title: Estimated usage by model (last 2 days)

targets.query:
import "join"

data = from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_use" and r._field == "pct")

top = data
  |> group(columns: ["project"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> top(n: 8, columns: ["_value"])
  |> keep(columns: ["project"])

join.inner(left: data |> group(), right: top, on: (l, r) => l.project == r.project, as: (l, r) => l)
  |> group(columns: ["project"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 10m, fn: sum, createEmpty: true)
  |> fill(column: "_value", value: 0.0)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "project"])

panels.title: 5-hour windows per 7-day window, by how full they got
panels.description: How many 5-hour windows ran in each 7-day window (last 8 weeks), split by the highest utilization each reached: full (90%+, it ran out or nearly), mostly, partial, or barely used (under 10%, e.g. a window started only to keep the clock going). More windows and more of them full is the goal. The current week is still filling and the oldest may be cut off.

targets.query:
import "array"
import "date"
import "internal/debug"

windows = from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_usage" and r.provider == "claude" and (r._field == "u5" or r._field == "reset5" or r._field == "reset7"))
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.u5 and exists r.reset5 and exists r.reset7)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with win: int(v: r.reset5 / 600.0 + 0.5)}))
  |> group(columns: ["win"])
  |> max(column: "u5")
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: 1, win: r.win, peak: r.u5, wreset: r.reset5, week: int(v: r.reset7 / 43200.0 + 0.5)}))

pings = from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -1y)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_event" and r.provider == "claude" and r.kind == "ping" and r._field == "reset")
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: 1, preset: r._value}))

firstEvent = from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -1y)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "defenestrator_event" and r._field == "reason")
  |> group()
  |> first()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: 1, since: float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0}))

withPings = union(tables: [pings, array.from(rows: [{k: 1, preset: 0.0}])])

matched = join(tables: {w: windows, p: withPings}, on: ["k"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({k: r.k, win: r.win, peak: r.peak, wreset: r.wreset, week: r.week, hit: if r.preset > 0.0 and r.preset - r.wreset < 1800.0 and r.wreset - r.preset < 1800.0 then 1 else 0}))
  |> group(columns: ["win"])
  |> max(column: "hit")
  |> group()

// who started each window: defenestrator (a ping's reset matches this window's), you (events were
// being logged and no ping matches), or unknown (the window is from before events were logged)
classified = join(tables: {a: matched, b: firstEvent}, on: ["k"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({win: r.win, peak: r.peak, week: r.week, start: r.wreset - 18000.0,
      who: if r.hit == 1 then "defenestrator" else if r.wreset - 18000.0 >= r.since then "you" else "unknown"}))

classified
  |> map(fn: (r) => {
      end = time(v: r.week * 43200 * 1000000000)
      day = date.truncate(t: end, unit: 1d)
      names = ["Sun", "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat"]
      return {week: r.week, label: "ends " + names[date.weekDay(t: day)] + " " + string(v: date.month(t: day)) + "/" + string(v: date.monthDay(t: day)),
        full: if r.peak >= 90.0 then 1 else 0, mostly: if r.peak >= 50.0 and r.peak < 90.0 then 1 else 0,
        partial: if r.peak >= 10.0 and r.peak < 50.0 then 1 else 0, barely: if r.peak < 10.0 then 1 else 0}
    })
  |> group(columns: ["week", "label"])
  |> reduce(identity: {full: 0, mostly: 0, partial: 0, barely: 0}, fn: (r, accumulator) => ({full: accumulator.full + r.full, mostly: accumulator.mostly + r.mostly, partial: accumulator.partial + r.partial, barely: accumulator.barely + r.barely}))
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["week"])
  |> rename(columns: {full: "full (90%+)", mostly: "mostly (50-90%)", partial: "partial (10-50%)", barely: "barely used (<10%)"})
  |> keep(columns: ["label", "full (90%+)", "mostly (50-90%)", "partial (10-50%)", "barely used (<10%)"])

panels.title: How full each 5-hour window got
panels.description: One bar per 5-hour window, placed where it started, as tall as the highest 5-hour utilization reached in it (a bar at 100 ran out). Colour is what started the window: orange is the defenestrator, blue is your own first message, grey is from before events were logged (so unknown). The same colours mark the start on the 5-hour, model and project charts above. Lines up with the 7-day chart: see where each week's windows fall.
